original_question: What is the precise relationship among ample fields, virtually ample fields, and weakly ample fields? In particular, if a field K is called virtually ample when some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample when every K-curve C becomes infinite over some finite extension L/K, must every weakly ample field be virtually ample, and must every virtually ample field already be ample?
target_in_paper: Section 5, “Virtually ample fields”: the paired open questions asking whether every weakly ample field is virtually ample and whether every virtually ample field is ample.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It identifies the right three notions, uses the correct finite-extension language for “virtually ample,” uses the curve-after-finite-extension infinitude condition for “weakly ample,” and asks exactly the two implication questions that Section 5 is concerned with.
missing_details: The paper’s basic ambient objects are fields and K-curves, where the curve notion used in this context is the standard one from the paper’s background: a smooth geometrically integral curve over K.
To make the question stand alone, you should state the curve criterion for ampleness used in the paper: K is ample iff every K-curve with a K-rational point has infinitely many K-rational points.
In the weakly ample condition, the finite extension L/K is allowed to depend on the curve C; this quantifier should be explicit.
The paper asks these as two specific implication questions, not as a broader classification problem about the full lattice of relationships among the three classes.
No extra hypotheses on K (such as characteristic restrictions, perfection, Hilbertianity, or Galois assumptions on L/K) are part of the question and should not be added.

If you use the variety-based definition of ample instead of the curve criterion, you should explicitly say: for every geometrically integral K-variety with a smooth K-point, the set of K-points is Zariski-dense.
refined_question: Let K be a field. Recall that K is called ample if every smooth geometrically integral K-curve over K that has a K-rational point in fact has infinitely many K-rational points. Define K to be virtually ample if some finite extension of K is ample, and weakly ample if for every smooth geometrically integral K-curve C/K there exists a finite extension L/K, depending on C, such that C(L) is infinite. Is every weakly ample field virtually ample? Is every virtually ample field ample?
justification: This rewrite stays tightly aligned with the paper’s Section 5. Your draft was already aimed at the correct open problem, but the paper formulates it as two concrete implication questions rather than as a broad request for the “precise relationship” among three classes. The only substantive additions needed to make the question self-contained are the paper’s standard curve criterion for ampleness and the explicit quantifier that the finite extension in the weakly ample condition may depend on the curve.
